# Specification: Crew Chatter MVP

## Summary

Crew Chatter is a single-user note web application. This specification covers the MVP described in the design: email/password authentication with per-user data isolation, note creation and editing with debounced auto-save, a notes dashboard, nested folders, color-coded tags, full-text search, pinning, archive and trash with restore, checklists, attachments, version history, export and import, and responsive desktop and mobile layouts.

Criterion AC-007 from the earlier draft (single-use password-reset tokens) was withdrawn because the design does not state it. Its ID is retired and is not reused.

## Technical approach

- Stack already present in the repository: an npm workspaces monorepo with `backend/` (Express + TypeScript + PostgreSQL via `pg`) and `frontend/` (React 18 + Vite + Tailwind + TipTap + TanStack Query + Zustand + Radix UI).
- The plan uses only dependencies already in `package-lock.json`: `bcryptjs` (password hashing), `jsonwebtoken` (sessions), `multer` (uploads and imports), `archiver` (ZIP export), `pdfkit` (PDF export), `uuid`, and `pg` on the backend; TipTap, Radix UI, TanStack Query, Zustand, and `clsx` on the frontend.
- Schema creation lives in a TypeScript migration module run at backend startup. The tables follow the design's suggested data model, plus a password-reset token table and a note activity table.
- Note bodies are stored as TipTap JSON with a derived plain-text column. Search uses a PostgreSQL full-text index over the title and that plain text.
- Checklist items are stored as `ChecklistItem` rows and edited in a checklist panel inside the note editor; AC-051 covers the design's checklist editing, so AC-012 lists the remaining editor formats.
- Production code is organized by feature under `src/features/`, with shared code in `src/lib/` and `src/components/`, as `.claude/CLAUDE.md` directs.
- In this repository, `npm run typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` over `backend/src`, `npm run lint` runs ESLint over `backend/src` and `frontend/src`, and `npm run build` runs `tsc` for the backend and `tsc && vite build` for the frontend. Every declared source file sits under one of those `src` directories, and both workspaces emit build output to `dist/`, which `.gitignore` ignores.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-001: Submitting the registration form with an email address that has no account and a password creates an account and signs the user in to an empty dashboard.
- AC-002: Submitting the registration form with an email address that already has an account is rejected with an error message and creates no second account.
- AC-003: Signing in with a registered email and its correct password opens that user's dashboard, and signing in with an incorrect password shows an error message and does not sign the user in.
- AC-004: After the user clicks "Sign out", reloading the application shows the sign-in screen and API requests for notes from that browser return HTTP 401.
- AC-005: The stored password value in every user row is a bcrypt hash and never equals the plaintext password that was submitted.
- AC-006: Completing the password-reset flow with a valid reset token and a new password lets the user sign in with the new password, and signing in with the old password is rejected.
- AC-008: When user B requests a note, folder, tag, checklist item, attachment, version, or export belonging to user A by its id, the API responds with HTTP 404 and returns none of user A's data.
- AC-009: List, filter, and search responses for user B never include notes, folders, tags, or attachments owned by user A.
- AC-010: Clicking "New note" on the dashboard opens the editor for a new note with keyboard focus in its title field or its body field.
- AC-011: A note's title, body, created_at, updated_at, folder assignment, tags, pinned state, archived state, and checklist items each persist after a page reload.
- AC-012: The editor can apply headings, bold, italic, bulleted lists, numbered lists, links, block quotes, and code blocks, and each applied format is still present after the note is reloaded.
- AC-013: Pasting HTML copied from a web page that contains a heading, bold text, italic text, a bulleted list, and a link into the editor keeps each of them as the corresponding editor format.
- AC-014: A note whose title and body contain emoji, CJK characters, and accented Latin characters shows identical characters after saving and reloading.
- AC-015: While the user types with gaps under 500 ms between keystrokes no save request is sent, and a save request carrying the latest content is sent no earlier than 500 ms and no later than 1,000 ms after the last keystroke.
- AC-016: The note editor has no manual save button, and an edit is present after reloading the page once the save indicator shows "Saved".
- AC-017: The save indicator shows "Saving" while a save request is in flight, "Saved" after it succeeds, "Unable to save" after the server responds with an error, and "Offline" while the browser reports no network connection.
- AC-018: While an edit is unsaved or a save request is pending, closing or reloading the browser tab triggers the browser's leave-page confirmation prompt.
- AC-019: Opening a different note or view inside the application while an edit is unsaved saves that edit first, so reopening the original note shows the edit.
- AC-020: A note saved with an empty title is shown with the label "Untitled note" in note lists, search results, and the editor.
- AC-021: The dashboard shows a section of pinned notes and a list of recent notes ordered by last updated date with the newest first.
- AC-022: The note list offers sorting by last updated date, creation date, title, and pinned status, and choosing each option reorders the list by that key.
- AC-023: Each note card or row shows the note's title, a preview of its body text, its tags, its folder name, and its last updated timestamp.
- AC-024: A signed-in user with zero notes sees an empty state on the dashboard that contains an action which creates their first note.
- AC-025: A user can create a top-level folder and a subfolder inside any existing folder, and the sidebar folder tree shows each subfolder nested under its parent.
- AC-026: Renaming a folder updates its name in the sidebar and on the cards of notes it contains, and the new name persists after a reload.
- AC-027: Changing a folder's position among its sibling folders in the sidebar persists the new order after a reload.
- AC-028: Each folder that has subfolders has a toggle in the sidebar tree that hides and shows its subfolders.
- AC-029: Deleting a folder that contains notes opens a dialog offering to move those notes to another chosen folder or leave them uncategorized, and after confirmation the notes are in the chosen folder or have no folder respectively.
- AC-030: A user can add more than one tag to a note, and one tag can be applied to multiple notes.
- AC-031: A user can assign a color to a tag, and that color is shown on the tag wherever the tag is displayed.
- AC-032: Renaming a tag changes the displayed name on every note carrying it, and deleting a tag removes it from every note without deleting those notes.
- AC-033: Creating a tag, or renaming a tag, to a name that matches another of the same user's tags when letter case is ignored is rejected with an error message, while a different user can create a tag with that name.
- AC-034: Typing part of a tag's name in the tag picker lists the user's tags whose names contain the typed text.
- AC-035: Selecting a tag in the sidebar shows exactly the user's notes that carry that tag.
- AC-036: Pressing Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux, or Cmd+K on macOS, anywhere in the signed-in application opens global search with keyboard focus in the search field.
- AC-037: Global search returns notes whose title or body contains the entered keyword and does not return notes that contain it in neither.
- AC-038: Each search result shows a text snippet in which the matched keyword is wrapped in a highlight element.
- AC-039: Search results can be narrowed by folder, tag, date range, note status (active or archived), and attachment presence, and each applied filter removes results that do not match it.
- AC-040: A pinned note appears in the dashboard's pinned section and, in its folder view sorted by last updated date, before every unpinned note.
- AC-041: Pinned notes in note lists display a pin indicator that unpinned notes do not display.
- AC-042: Unpinning a note removes it from the dashboard's pinned section and removes its pin indicator.
- AC-043: A "Pinned" sidebar destination lists exactly the user's pinned notes that are neither archived nor trashed.
- AC-044: Archiving a note removes it from the dashboard, folder views, tag views, and the "Pinned" destination, and filtering the note list to archived notes lists it.
- AC-045: Moving a note to trash removes it from every view except Trash, and the Trash view lists it.
- AC-046: Clicking "Restore" on a trashed note returns it to its previous folder when that folder still exists, otherwise to the uncategorized notes, and shows a confirmation message.
- AC-047: A trashed note that has been in trash for less than the retention period can be restored, and a trashed note that has been in trash for longer than the retention period is permanently deleted by the purge process and no longer listed in Trash.
- AC-048: Permanently deleting a note requires confirming a dialog whose text states that the note cannot be recovered and whose confirm button is labeled "Delete permanently".
- AC-049: After a note is permanently deleted, no API endpoint returns the note, its checklist items, its attachments, or its versions.
- AC-050: Folder deletion, tag deletion, and permanent note deletion each open a confirmation dialog before anything is deleted, and each dialog's confirm button label contains the word "Delete" and is not "OK".
- AC-051: Within the note editor the user can add checklist items and mark each one complete or incomplete without leaving the editor, and each item's state persists after a reload.
- AC-052: In the note editor, a note with at least one checklist item shows progress in the form "N of M complete", where N is the number of completed items and M is the total number of items.
- AC-053: The "Open tasks" filter lists exactly the user's notes that have at least one incomplete checklist item.
- AC-054: Note lists can be filtered by folder, tag, pinned state, archived state, task completion state, and date range, and each filter shows only the notes that match it.
- AC-055: Uploading a file of a supported type within the size limit to a note shows the attachment with its file name, size, upload time, and a control that downloads or opens it.
- AC-056: An attached image of a supported image type is displayed as an inline preview inside the note.
- AC-057: Uploading a file larger than the size limit or of an unsupported type is rejected, stores nothing, and shows the user an error message stating which of the two reasons applied.
- AC-058: Requesting an attachment download without a signed-in session returns HTTP 401, and requesting it as a user who does not own the note returns HTTP 404.
- AC-059: Saving a content change that meets the version-creation rule decided under OD-004 adds a new entry to the note's version history, and saving a change that does not meet that rule adds no entry.
- AC-060: The version history lists each version with its timestamp and a change preview whose content follows the decision recorded under OD-022.
- AC-061: Restoring a prior version makes its title and body the note's current content, adds a new version with a higher version number than any existing version, and keeps every earlier version in the history.
- AC-062: Exporting a note as Markdown downloads a .md file in which the note's headings, bold, italic, lists, links, block quotes, and code blocks are written in Markdown syntax.
- AC-063: Exporting a note as plain text downloads a .txt file containing the note's title and body text without formatting markup.
- AC-064: Exporting a note as PDF downloads a file served with Content-Type application/pdf whose content begins with "%PDF".
- AC-065: Exporting the entire collection downloads a ZIP archive that contains one Markdown file for each of the user's active and archived notes, one for each trashed note only if the decision under OD-023 includes trashed notes, and every attachment file belonging to the exported notes.
- AC-066: Importing supported files first shows a review step that reports the number of notes, folders, tags, and attachments that will be created, and nothing is created until the user confirms.
- AC-067: After the user confirms an import, the numbers of notes, folders, tags, and attachments created equal the numbers shown in the review step.
- AC-068: Creating, updating, archiving, restoring, and deleting a note each records an activity entry containing the event type and the time of the event.
- AC-069: At a viewport width of 1280 px, the left navigation sidebar, the note list, and the editor panel of an open note are all visible at the same time.
- AC-070: At a viewport width of 375 px, navigation is hidden behind a control that opens it as a drawer, and an open note's editor spans the viewport width with the note list hidden.
- AC-071: In the note list, ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the selection to the next and previous note, and Enter opens the selected note.
- AC-072: Every interactive control is reachable and operable with the keyboard alone, and the focused control shows a visible focus indicator.
- AC-073: Every icon-only button exposes an accessible name to screen readers through its text content or an aria-label attribute.
- AC-074: API responses with HTTP status 500 contain a generic error message and no stack trace, SQL text, or file system path.
- AC-075: API validation failures respond with HTTP 400 and a message naming the field that must be corrected.
- AC-076: API requests for notes, folders, tags, checklist items, attachments, versions, exports, and imports are rejected with HTTP 401 when no valid session is presented.
- AC-077: A note's versions within the retention limit decided under OD-005 remain listed in its version history, and versions beyond that limit are no longer listed.
- AC-078: Every clickable control is a native button, link, or form input element, or an element with an ARIA widget role such as button, link, checkbox, menuitem, tab, or treeitem.
- AC-079: Selecting a global search result opens that note in the editor.
- AC-080: Signing in, creating and editing a note, and finding that note through global search each complete without error in the current stable release of Safari on iOS and of Chrome on Android.
- AC-081: Importing a Markdown (.md) file and a plain-text (.txt) file, in the input form accepted under OD-007, creates one note for each file whose body contains that file's text, with Markdown syntax converted to editor formats.
- AC-082: Submitting the forgot-password form with the email address of a registered account starts a password reset for that account, with the reset token delivered as decided under OD-001, and shows the user a confirmation message.

## Open decisions

- OD-001 (high): How is a password-reset link or token delivered to the user, given that the repository has no email provider configured?
- OD-002 (high): What is the maximum attachment file size that the documented limit enforces, and where is that limit documented to users?
- OD-003 (high): Which file types (MIME types or extensions) are supported attachments beyond images, PDFs, and text files, which "common document formats" are included, and which image types get an inline preview?
- OD-004 (high): What content change counts as "meaningful" and creates a new version: every successful auto-save, a minimum time gap since the previous version, a minimum edit size, or something else?
- OD-005 (medium): How many historical versions are kept per note, or for how long are they kept?
- OD-006 (medium): What is the trash retention period, and who configures it: each user in their settings, or the operator through server configuration?
- OD-007 (high): What input does import accept (individual .md and .txt files, a ZIP such as the full-collection export, or both), how is each imported note's title derived, and how are folders, tags, and attachments derived from the imported content?
- OD-008 (medium): Does "private object storage" for attachments require an S3-compatible object store, which needs a new dependency and configuration, or does a private server-side directory served only through authorized endpoints satisfy it?
- OD-009 (medium): When a folder that contains subfolders is deleted, what happens to those subfolders and the notes inside them?
- OD-010 (medium): What latency bound, percentile, and measurement conditions (hardware, network, dataset) define search returning results "within approximately one second" for up to 10,000 notes per user?
- OD-011 (low): What latency bound and network conditions define the 200 ms UI response target for note creation and editing actions?
- OD-012 (low): How are relevance and recency combined to rank search results?
- OD-013 (low): Which keyboard shortcut creates a new note, and can the user change it?
- OD-014 (low): Does the date-range filter apply to a note's creation date, its last updated date, or a user-selectable one of the two?
- OD-015 (low): Which export actions count as privacy-sensitive and therefore require a confirmation step before they run?
- OD-016 (low): When a search result is opened, what does landing "at the matching content" require, such as scrolling to and highlighting the first match, and in which cases is it not required?
- OD-017 (low): What contrast ratio counts as sufficient color contrast, for example WCAG 2.2 AA at 4.5:1 for body text?
- OD-018 (low): What behavior does keyboard support for "saving focus transitions" require?
- OD-019 (low): Which document editors' pasted content must the editor accept (for example Microsoft Word or Google Docs), and must pasted formatting be preserved or only the text?
- OD-020 (low): Which quick-access controls must the dashboard display?
- OD-021 (medium): Do pinned notes stay above unpinned notes in the dashboard and folder views under every sort order, or only under particular sort orders, given that pinned status is also offered as a sort option?
- OD-022 (low): Does a version's change preview show that version's title and body, or the difference from the version before it?
- OD-023 (low): Does the full-collection export include notes that are currently in trash?
- OD-024 (medium): Are HTTPS transport, regular backups, and backup restoration procedures delivered by this feature through code, configuration, or documentation in this repository, or provided by the hosting environment outside this feature?
- OD-025 (low): Which desktop browsers count as the "major desktop browsers" the UI must support?

## Out of scope

- Google sign-in and other OAuth providers (named in the design as a future enhancement).
- Team collaboration, commenting, workspace administration, native offline-first mobile apps, word-processor-style layout, project management features, and public publishing (design non-goals).
- Product success metrics and analytics instrumentation. The design lists metrics but states no behavior or instrumentation requirement for them.
- Visual tone and typographic feel ("calm, focused, and lightweight", "generous line height", "restrained formatting controls", "subtle" saved indicator) are design guidance with no checkable part.
- The 10-second note-creation goal is a success metric; AC-010 covers its checkable part, a single action that opens a focused editor.

pieces.title: Authentication, note editing with auto-save, dashboard shell, and responsive layout
Nested folders, color-coded tags, pinning, and dashboard sorting
Archive, trash with restore and purge, checklists, note filters, and activity tracking
Note attachments in private storage and version history with restore
Global search, export and import, and per-user isolation across every resource
Keyboard operability, screen-reader names, semantic controls, and mobile-browser support across the app

split.rationale:
The specification declares 64 files, which is more than one run can build, so it is split into six features of 17 to 29 distinct files each. Each feature builds only on the ones before it.

1. Foundation comes first because everything else needs it: the server, database pool, migrations, sessions, error handling, the notes API, the editor with debounced auto-save, the dashboard shell and the desktop and mobile layout.

2. Organization adds folders, tags and pinning on top of the notes API and sidebar. It also adds the shared ConfirmDialog. The pinned dashboard section and pinned sorting (AC-021, AC-022) belong here because they need pinning. Note cards showing tags and folder names (AC-023) need folders and tags.

3. Note lifecycle adds archive, trash, restore, the retention purge, checklists, list filters and the activity log. AC-011 (every note field persists) belongs here because checklist items and archived state appear only now. AC-068 (activity for archive, restore and delete) needs these actions. AC-050 (delete-confirmation dialogs) needs permanent deletion. AC-043 (Pinned excludes archived and trashed notes) needs archive and trash.

4. Attachments and versions extend the note editor and private storage. They also extend permanent deletion and the purge from feature 3, so AC-049 (a deleted note leaves no attachments or versions) can be checked here.

5. Search, export and import come after attachments for three reasons. The search filter for attachment presence (AC-039) needs attachments. The ZIP export (AC-065) bundles attachment files. Isolation and 401 checks (AC-008, AC-009, AC-076) cover attachments, versions, exports and imports, so they can only be checked once all of these exist. This feature also confirms that search leaves out trashed notes (AC-045 from feature 3). AC-020 (Untitled note label) is placed here because the label must also appear in search results.

6. Accessibility is last. AC-072, AC-073 and AC-078 apply to every interactive control, and AC-080 runs a flow through global search on mobile browsers. All of that can only be checked once every frontend component exists.
